summary:
The bill, the Legislative Branch Appropriations Act, 2025, appropriates funds from the Treasury not otherwise appropriated for the legislative branch for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2025, and enacts related substantive provisions.

Title I provides appropriations for the House of Representatives, including $1,932,655,000 for salaries and expenses, with specified allocations for leadership offices, Members’ Representational Allowances ($843,605,000), intern allowances under 2 U.S.C. § 5322a and 2 U.S.C. § 5106, committee employees, officers and employees, and allowances and expenses; and a $10,000,000 House Modernization Initiatives Account under 2 U.S.C. § 5513. Administrative provisions in Title I include: section 110, requiring unexpended Members’ Representational Allowance balances to be deposited for deficit or debt reduction; section 111, limiting vehicle lease payments from the MRA to $1,000 per month; section 112, imposing minimization procedures on federal entities providing cybersecurity assistance to the House; section 113, amending 42 U.S.C. § 13212(f) to remove a House exemption from long-term lease requirements, effective FY2025 and each succeeding fiscal year; and section 114, amending 2 U.S.C. § 2062(d)(3) to permit use of the Child Care Center Revolving Fund for telecom expenses, effective FY2025 and thereafter.

Joint items appropriate funds for the Joint Economic Committee, Joint Committee on Taxation, Office of the Attending Physician, and Office of Congressional Accessibility Services. For the Capitol Police, the bill appropriates $619,257,000 for salaries and $213,158,000 for general expenses, with a proviso that basic training costs at FLETC be paid by DHS. Section 115 amends 5 U.S.C. § 4120 to require Capitol Police Board approval for international training, effective FY2025 and thereafter.

Further appropriations are made for the Office of Congressional Workplace Rights ($8,150,000), Congressional Budget Office ($73,259,000, with a directive to spend at least $500,000 on transparency improvements), and the Architect of the Capitol across multiple accounts (Capitol Building, Capitol Grounds, House Office Buildings, Capitol Power Plant, Library Buildings and Grounds, Capitol Police Buildings/Grounds/Security, Botanic Garden, and Capitol Visitor Center). Section 116 prohibits incentive payments to contractors behind schedule or over budget. Section 117 authorizes the Architect to enter cooperative agreements and engage in plant material exchanges for the Capitol Grounds and Arboretum, effective FY2025 and thereafter.

For the Library of Congress, the bill appropriates $617,000,000 for salaries and expenses; $105,642,000 for the Copyright Office (offset by collections); $141,487,000 for the Congressional Research Service; and $65,205,000 for the National Library Service for the Blind and Print Disabled. Section 118 caps obligational authority for reimbursable and revolving fund activities at $328,789,000. The Government Publishing Office receives appropriations for Congressional Publishing ($83,000,000), Public Information Programs ($41,664,000), and the Business Operations Revolving Fund ($11,425,000). The Government Accountability Office receives $896,700,000. The Congressional Office for International Leadership Fund receives $6,600,000, with restrictions on Russian participants, and the John C. Stennis Center receives $430,000.

Title II—General Provisions—includes: section 202, limiting obligation availability to FY2025 unless otherwise provided; section 209, prohibiting procurement and use of covered telecommunications equipment or services (Huawei, ZTE, Hytera, Hikvision, Dahua, and foreign adversary-controlled entities), with phased effective dates (FY2025 for direct procurement, FY2026 for contracts with entities using such equipment) and a one-time waiver authority; section 210, exempting the GPO Director and Librarian of Congress from statutory pay freezes; section 211, amending 5 U.S.C. § 13144 to exclude Member-provided medical or dental care from the definition of a fiduciary relationship, effective FY2025 and thereafter; section 212, prohibiting funds for diversity, equity, and inclusion training promoting divisive concepts; section 213, prohibiting discriminatory actions based on religious belief or moral conviction regarding marriage as a union of one man and one woman; section 214, barring cost-of-living adjustments for Members under 2 U.S.C. § 4501 in FY2025; and section 215, a spending reduction account of $0. Additional provisions address private vehicle maintenance, consulting services transparency, Legislative Branch Financial Managers Council cost-sharing, transfer limitations, Capitol tour protections, and computer network pornography blocking.
